subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For a Codex native thread that resumes but cannot start an OpenClaw turn, should Gateway force-rotate automatically, fail the accepted send visibly, or add a health/doctor recovery path before accepting more sends?
rationale: Current code has plausible mitigations but the durable user contract for `chat.send` success versus Codex native-thread liveness is a product/API decision, not a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Visible failure plus bounded recovery
options.body: Return or broadcast a visible failure when a send cannot start a turn, and force-rotate only for source-proven stale or oversized native bindings.

options.title: Aggressive automatic rotation
options.body: Clear and restart Codex native bindings whenever resume or turn/start liveness is suspect, accepting possible loss of warm-thread efficiency.

options.title: Health-only recovery surface
options.body: Keep immediate ACK behavior but add audit/doctor/session reset tooling so users can recover wedged native threads manually.

recommendation.title: Visible failure plus bounded recovery
recommendation.body: Return or broadcast a visible failure when a send cannot start a turn, and force-rotate only for source-proven stale or oversized native bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most recent merged Codex native overflow rotation path that would likely anchor the recovery contract.
